description: Hi, I’m Connor! I’m a Health Science student at CSUCI with a unique blend of experience in web development, healthcare research, and competitive esports. My interests lie at the intersection of technology, human performance, and making complex information highly accessible.
summary:
On Mars, CURIOSITY sparks discovery, every OPPORTUNITY carries a cost, & survival takes SPIRIT & PERSEVERANCE.

Sol Survivor starts with a landing in Gale Crater, followed by explorer discoveries, building a base & keeping your astronauts alive. M.A.R.V., a friendly robot guide, introduces one action at a time. Storm warnings, crew needs, collectible discoveries & short science quizzes turn each mission into an OPPORTUNITY for planning, prioritizing & adapting.

NASA Open Science Data Repository study records, Curiosity mission resources, radiation research & historical dust-storm reports inform the experience. Sources are traceable, gameplay simplifications are explained, & solar events remain clearly labeled practice storms while historical downloads are unavailable.

The mission: reward curiosity & clever choices, all while sneaking in real NASA science & fascinating Mars facts into a replayable game anyone would become captured by.
details:
Sol Survivor is a Mars survival game where players explore Gale Crater, build an outpost, manage resources & care for astronauts through a 30-sol mission. Along the way, discoveries, unexpected events & scientific trivia turn curiosity into part of the adventure.

The challenge is deciding what needs attention next. An astronaut sent exploring cannot also be producing oxygen or building a room. A tired crew needs rest, even when there is work to finish. Shielding needs power, while dust storms threaten the supply. Players experiment, see the consequences of their choices & return with a different plan.

The game uses moments that naturally make players curious as opportunities to teach. When a solar flare or another new event appears, the player has a reason to ask: What is happening? Why does it matter? What should I do? Short explanations connect the science to what is about to happen in the game. Quizzes then ask players to use that information, encouraging them to pay attention instead of clicking through every message to get back to playing.

Exploration rewards players with scientific information, including discoveries connected to Curiosity’s work in Gale Crater. M.A.R.V., a friendly robot guide, introduces actions one at a time. Collectible discoveries, repeated encounters with scientific ideas, changing events & different strategies give players reasons to return, practice what they remember & discover something new.

NASA Open Science Data Repository study records, Mars mission resources, radiation research & historical dust-storm reports provide scientific context. The game distinguishes those sources from simplified gameplay rules. Solar events are labeled practice storms where historical event records are unavailable.

I created Sol Survivor as a solo participant, directing its concept, gameplay & revisions. Claude assisted with coding, SVG artwork & programmed sound effects. Google Gemini was used to create all of the music. The game uses TypeScript & React, with Vite for building the website. GitHub stores the project, GitHub Actions builds & deploys updates, & GitHub Pages hosts the playable game. ChatGPT assisted with troubleshooting & submission preparation.

My design priorities were curiosity, replayability, understandable choices & an experience that feels rewarding to play. Browser access, gradual guidance & plain language help make the game approachable for its intended audience.

I have always loved games that let me practice something repeatedly while picking up new knowledge along the way. Learning something new is one of the greatest treasures we can have. With Sol Survivor, I wanted that treasure to be waiting around the next crater.
